# Versioned browser libraries

This shelf lets imported games retain their requested engine version and
renderer. It is separate from the patched shared stack at `/lib/three/`,
`/lib/rapier/` and `/lib/kit/`; existing games keep using those paths.

## Available releases

Three.js includes **every stable release and patch** in the requested range:

`0.180.0`, `0.181.0`, `0.181.1`, `0.181.2`, `0.182.0`, `0.183.0`, `0.183.1`,
`0.183.2`, `0.184.0`, `0.185.0`, `0.185.1`, `0.186.0`, `0.186.1`.

Each is the full official npm package: classic WebGL and WebGPU builds, TSL,
all addons, source modules, fonts, Draco and Basis decoders, and the license.
The versioned packages are upstream distributions, without the shared stack's
local patches or WebGL-only exclusions.

The shelf also pins **Three.js 0.160.0** and older **Rapier 3D compat** releases:
**0.14.0** for The Ash-Bound Prophecy and **0.19.0** for Ashbound: The Sleeper’s
Oath. These are full official packages, preserved on every sync so the games
retain their original WebGL renderer and physics.
The r160 browser fixture exercises classic WebGL and addons; newer releases
also exercise the modern WebGPU build and TSL.

Rapier includes **0.19.3, 0.20.0 and 0.21.0** for all 12 official packages:

| Dimension | Standard | SIMD | Deterministic |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2D | `rapier2d`, `rapier2d-compat` | `rapier2d-simd`, `rapier2d-simd-compat` | `rapier2d-deterministic`, `rapier2d-deterministic-compat` |
| 3D | `rapier3d`, `rapier3d-compat` | `rapier3d-simd`, `rapier3d-simd-compat` | `rapier3d-deterministic`, `rapier3d-deterministic-compat` |

All package names have the `@dimforge/` scope. Stable releases are included;
nightly/canary builds are outside this shelf. The starting version `0.193`
was interpreted as the published release `0.19.3`.

## Importing games

Use `pnpm ingest <file|folder|zip>`. The importer rewrites recognized Three.js
and Rapier URLs in HTML, JavaScript and CSS to local paths. Supported hosts:
jsDelivr (npm and Three.js GitHub tags), unpkg, esm.sh, Skypack, JSPM, cdnjs,
and the official Three.js build/examples paths.

Exact version pins stay exact. Partial versions and `^0.x`/`~0.x` ranges select
a compatible local patch. Unmapped bare imports use the detected package
version, or the latest version in `manifest.json` when none is specified;
unversioned CDN references also use the latest. The importer adds per-version
import-map scopes so addons and TSL resolve their own version of Three.js.
Existing mappings, game assets, embedded bundles and game logic are retained.
The dry-run report lists dependencies that would become local. Re-importing
the same input still skips it as a duplicate.

Unavailable releases and files are reported and left unchanged. A URL for an
old global `three.min.js` build is not silently replaced by an ES module:
those global builds are not part of r180 onward. Arbitrary missing game files,
other libraries, custom CDN-generated bundles, or incompatible game code still
need individual attention. Installing engines cannot supply missing models,
textures, levels or audio.

## Manual paths

Three.js packages preserve the npm layout:

```text
/lib/vendor/three/0.180.0/build/three.module.js
/lib/vendor/three/0.180.0/build/three.webgpu.js
/lib/vendor/three/0.180.0/build/three.tsl.js
/lib/vendor/three/0.180.0/examples/jsm/loaders/GLTFLoader.js
/lib/vendor/three/0.180.0/examples/jsm/libs/draco/gltf/draco_decoder.wasm
```

A manually copied classic WebGL game can use:

```html
<script type="importmap">
{
  "imports": {
    "three": "/lib/vendor/three/0.180.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/webgpu": "/lib/vendor/three/0.180.0/build/three.webgpu.js",
    "three/tsl": "/lib/vendor/three/0.180.0/build/three.tsl.js",
    "three/addons/": "/lib/vendor/three/0.180.0/examples/jsm/"
  }
}
</script>
```

Place the import map before module scripts and module preloads. Serve the repo
root over HTTP; opening an HTML file through `file://` does not resolve `/lib/`.
With multiple versions, use the per-package `scopes` generated by the importer.
It also adds local mappings for pinned third-party addon imports: OpenType,
Lottie and MP4Box, whose ESM files and licenses live in `extras/`.

Rapier package files preserve their upstream paths, including separate WASM:

```text
/lib/vendor/rapier/0.19.3/rapier3d-compat/rapier.mjs
/lib/vendor/rapier/0.21.0/rapier3d-simd-compat/dist/rapier.mjs
/lib/vendor/rapier/0.21.0/rapier3d/rapier_wasm3d_bg.wasm
/lib/vendor/rapier/0.21.0/rapier3d/browser.mjs
```

The ordinary Rapier packages target bundlers and use extensionless imports and
direct WASM imports. Their additional `browser.mjs` entry re-exports and
initializes the **same version and physics flavor** of the official compat
package. Use that entry for native browser imports. Compat entries require
`await RAPIER.init()` before creating a world. The manifest records each
package's upstream entry and browser entry; they differ between releases.

## Refreshing and verifying

```bash
pnpm libraries:sync         # fetch current stable releases, with an npm integrity check
pnpm libraries:check        # verify every file hash, WASM binary and Rapier physics variant
pnpm test                  # importer and existing repository regressions
node scripts/check-libraries.mjs --browser-fixture
pnpm dev
```

The last two commands create and serve an ignored browser fixture at
`/.cache/libraries/browser-check.html`. It exercises every Three.js release
with classic WebGL and node rendering, TSL and representative addons, and runs
physics in every Rapier package. Add `?backend=webgpu` for the native WebGPU
path on a browser with a WebGPU adapter. The result is in `window.__libraryCheck`.

`scripts/vendor-libraries.mjs` downloads packages without installing them or
running lifecycle scripts. It checks npm's tarball integrity before extracting
them. `manifest.json` records source tarballs, versions, entry points and
SHA-256 hashes for the vendored files. Download caches and browser artifacts
stay under `.cache/libraries/`, outside version control and deployment. Run
the script without `--refresh` to reproduce the cached release set; refreshing
to new releases also requires extending the explicit verification matrix.
